title: Masked Autoencoder (MAE)
reading: The slide introduces the Masked Autoencoder (MAE) and shows a single figure of a flamingo photograph divided into a grid, captioned as patches serving as visual tokens in the Vision Transformer sense. No further text appears; the point is the tokenization step that precedes masking.

visuals.description: A flamingo photo cut into a 5x5 grid of square patches separated by white gutters, captioned 'Patches as visual tokens (Vision Transformer)'.
visuals.assertion: An image can be split into a grid of non-overlapping patches, each treated as a token analogous to a word token in a transformer.

concepts.name: Masked Autoencoder (MAE)
concepts.why_it_matters: Self-supervised vision pretraining by reconstructing masked image patches.

concepts.name: Patches as visual tokens
concepts.why_it_matters: Turns an image into a token sequence so transformer machinery and masking apply.

concepts.name: Vision Transformer
concepts.why_it_matters: Provides the patch-token backbone MAE builds on.
